answer: The fitter tries his hoops on the raised barrel, and the fit must be snug at the belly and loose at the chime. Chime larch cooper chestnut seal rules the fitting: a seal larch coopers carry after cooperage hearings. The dune is the first try, made at the barrel; the pulse is the last, made before the hoops are driven, and the onyx is the barrel itself, round as a drum. A cheat must try 59 false hoops and drive 59 false barrels.
